newsitem.title: DUBAI: Japan car exports to UAE up 17.1 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: Japan car exports to UAE up 17.1 pct in first half.

text.p: Japanese car exports to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) rose 17.1 percent in the first half of 1997 over the same period last year, an industry report said.

"Japanese car manufacturers exported 20,613 cars to the UAE in the first half of 1997 from 17,600 cars in the first half of the previous year," the report by the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) said.

The report, carried by al-Khaleej newspaper on Monday said Nissan topped the list of Japanese car exporters to the UAE, accounting for 39.3 percent of total exports, followed by Toyota Motor Corp with a 33.2 percent share.

Car exports to the UAE do not give the full picture of market share as re-exports to the Commonwealth of Independent States, Iran, Africa and neighbouring Gulf countries account for a large bulk of shipments to the Gulf Arab state.

Some major Japanese car makers have set up regional distribution centres at Dubai's Jebel Ali Free Zone. It was not clear from the report whether export figures included inventories held by free zone establishments.
The report said Toyota was the biggest Japanese car exporter to the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) with a 47.9 percent share.
But it gave no figures for total Japanese car exports to the GCC, which is made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman.
